price.a: Yes. Tomoru is free and open-source under GPL-3.0. The built-in cloud translation is free; cloud speech recognition uses your own API key, billed by the provider. Using only local engines is completely free.

systems.a: macOS 26 or later (Apple silicon), and Windows 11 (x64).

languages.a: Speech recognition supports up to 30 languages (depending on the chosen recognition engine), and translation supports 31 languages in any direction. The UI is available in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean.

setup.q: Do I need a virtual audio driver or microphone access?
setup.a: Neither. Tomoru captures your computer's audio directly and never uses the microphone.

blocked.q: Why does my system warn me on first launch?
blocked.a: Tomoru isn't notarized by Apple or signed for Windows yet. macOS: open System Settings › Privacy & Security, and click “Open Anyway” next to Tomoru. Windows: when SmartScreen warns, click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. Installing via terminal command skips these warnings on both macOS and Windows.

recording.q: Will subtitles show up in screen recordings or live streams?
recording.a: You can turn on “Hide subtitles from screen recording” in Settings so subtitles stay visible only to you.

meta.title: Tomoru: Live Subtitles & Real-Time Translation for Your PC
meta.description: Tomoru captures system audio and generates floating bilingual subtitles in real time. For live streams, anime, and games—if your computer plays sound, Tomoru translates it. Fully open-source and free on macOS and Windows.
meta.ogTitle: Tomoru: Live Subtitles for Anything You Watch
meta.ogDescription: Captures system audio and generates real-time floating bilingual subtitles. Live streams, anime, games—if there's sound, there are subtitles.

meta.ldDescription: Captures system audio directly and generates floating bilingual subtitles in real time. For live streams, anime, and games. Works offline or in the cloud.

overlay.title: Always on top, click-through
overlay.body: The subtitle window stays on top of your screen. Drag and resize freely; lock it to pass clicks through to what's behind, and automatically hide it from screen recordings and streams.

capture.artLabel: Listen to all system audio, or target a single app like a browser
capture.title: Native loopback, no microphone
capture.body: Captures system audio output directly without ever calling the microphone. Listen globally, or isolate a single app (like translating a stream in your browser while gaming).

engines.artLabel: Switch between local and cloud: data stays on your machine locally, or goes only to the chosen service
engines.localCaption: Audio and text stay on your device
engines.cloudCaption: Sent only to the service you choose
engines.title: Offline or cloud, switch as needed
engines.body: Speech recognition and translation can run entirely offline on your computer, keeping data private; or use built-in free cloud translation, or connect your own LLM API.

how.title: Hear, recognize, translate—sentence by sentence
how.lead: Speech recognition supports up to 30 languages (depending on the chosen recognition engine), and translation supports 31 languages. Original in white, translation in warm amber.

hear.title: Hear
hear.body: Captures system audio in real time, or targets a specific app.

recognize.title: Recognize
recognize.body: Streaming speech recognition generates the original text word by word as it's spoken.

translate.title: Translate
translate.body: Translations appear immediately in a floating bilingual overlay.

draft.title: No waiting for full sentences
draft.body: Displays an early draft of what's being said before the speaker pauses, then automatically updates to the full translation once the sentence finishes. Fast-paced streams stay in sync.
draft.artLabel: An early draft appears mid-sentence, then updates to the full translation when finished
draft.caption: See the draft first, updated to full when done

scenes.title: Proper names without translation blunders
scenes.body: Speech recognition easily mishears names as similar sounds, and machine translation loves literal guesses (like turning “クラウド” into “Crowd”). You can build a glossary for each anime or game you follow to fix homophones and keep names consistent. With your own API, it even learns new names from your subtitle history.
scenes.artLabel: Without a scene, メテオ is misheard as メデオ and クラウド is translated as Crowd; with the Final Fantasy VII scene, both original and translation are fixed
scenes.srcBefore: クラウド、<tspan class="bad">メデオ</tspan>が来る！
scenes.srcAfter: クラウド、<tspan class="good">メテオ</tspan>が来る！

picture.title: Select any silent text to translate
picture.body: For unvoiced dialogue, signs in videos, or stream chat, press <kbd>⌥⇧S</kbd> (<kbd>Alt+Shift+S</kbd> on Windows) and select a region on screen to translate it instantly. With local models, OCR runs entirely on your device.

start.title: Three steps to live subtitles

install.title: Download & run
install.body: Double-click the installer (if prompted, click “Open Anyway”); or run a single-line script in your terminal to skip security prompts.

choose.title: Choose language & engine
choose.body: Follow the first-run guide to pick spoken and target languages, and choose between offline local models or cloud APIs.

try.title: Quick trial, ready anytime
try.body: Play a sample to confirm subtitles appear properly. Tomoru sits quietly in the menu bar, ready to toggle anytime.

start.shotAlt: Tomoru first-run guide: Japanese to English selected, speech and translation engines picked, sample played with three checks passing, and shortcut tested
start.shotCaption: First-run guide: Settings › Try it out › Ready

privacy.title: Works offline, data stays on your device

mic.title: No microphone access
mic.body: Captures only internal system audio without requesting microphone permissions. Audio streams are discarded immediately after use.

local.title: On-device processing
local.body: With local engines, all processing happens on your computer. Even with cloud engines, data goes directly to the API service you specify.

history.title: History off by default
history.body: Subtitle history is disabled by default. If enabled, transcripts stay local on your machine and can be cleared with one click.

telemetry.title: Zero telemetry
telemetry.body: No user tracking or analytics. Aside from checking GitHub for updates and downloading models from open-source hosts, no data is sent anywhere.

mascot.alt: Tomoru: a girl with indigo hair and amber-tipped ends, looking up happily at Rubi the penguin perched on her head holding a paper lantern
mascot.title: A girl with a lantern, and a penguin on her head
mascot.name: The app is named after Tomoru (ともる), a girl holding a paper lantern: 灯る means “to light up.” The penguin on her head is ルビ (Rubi), named after ruby characters—the small pronunciation guides placed above difficult words to aid understanding.
mascot.tray: When not translating, they doze in the menu bar; when translation starts, they wake up together.
